occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During the course of the investigation, it was noted a toddler was unsupervised for approximately 2.5 minutes.

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Outdoor Activities: During the investigation, it was determined while viewing video footage that a child did not wash their hands upon entering the classroom from outside.

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During the investigation, it was determined that a 2-year-old child was left unattended on the playground for approximately 30 minutes.

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: At time of inspection, six out of seven monthly feeding instructions were not updated for the month of May.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Snug Fitting Sheets: At time of inspeciton, crib sheets were observed to not be tight-fitted.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Snug Fitting Sheets (26 TAC §746.2409(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR: At the time of the inspection, two out of the ten staff members did not have current CPR/First Aid certifications for review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR (26 TAC §746.1315(b))

occurrences.finding: Diaper Changing Equipment - Smooth, Non-absorbent, Easy to Clean Surface: The diaper changing mat in the infant room had two tears on the vinyl.     Note, a picture of the diaper changing mat was taken.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diaper Changing Equipment - Smooth, Non-absorbent, Easy to Clean Surface (26 TAC §746.3503(a))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: Several classrooms were observed of having the children's cots stored in the restroom. occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for: At the time of inspection the caregiver in the toddler room stated there were 18 children in her care when there were 16. NOTE: This was corrected when the caregiver recounted the children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Director Annual Training 30 Hours Required: The director did not have training certificates totaling 30 hours available for review.

occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Air Conditioners, Fans, Heaters Safeguarded (26 TAC §746.3701(3))

occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: Based upon information gathered and interviews conducted this incident was reported to Licensing more than two days after the incident occurring.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children: Based upon information gathered, surveillance and interviews conducted supervision was determined to have occurred when a child left the classroom to go into the gym unsupervised.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.violation_type_title: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent (26 TAC §746.707)

occurrences.finding: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk: Two of the four incident reports were unavailable for review.     NOTE: One of the two incident reports was corrected at inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.701(5))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children: Based upon information gathered, surveillance and interviews conducted inadequate supervision was determined to have occurred when children were left on the playground unsupervised as the caregiver went back into the classroom. In addition to several children running outside the classroom door into the playground unsupervised to get water bottles.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent: Two of the four children incident reports were not shared with the parents.      NOTE: One of the two was corrected at inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent (26 TAC §746.707)

occurrences.finding: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Hazards Removed or Repaired: There was a slide on the Pre-K playground that had half of the screws missing making the slide not secured in place.    Note: This was corrected at in inspection when the operation's maintenance personnel applied the screws to secure the slide in place.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Hazards Removed or Repaired (26 TAC §746.4751(c))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: In the course of this investigation, information gathered determined a lack of judgment by staff to immediately notify the parent of a child in distress. Parent was contacted approximately two hours after staff observed the child limping.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children: A child was not adequately supervised on the playground. They were able to leave their playground and reach a different one on the other side of the daycare and caregivers were not aware until the child was brought back by the director.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Based on information gathered, two caregivers did not use good judgement when it was decided to take an infant who was experiencing symptoms of allergic reaction to the child's relative who is an employee at the center versus following operational procedures and specific emergency instructions on the child's food allergy emergency plan such as immediately calling 911, administering epi-pen, keeping child warm, and avoiding unnecessary movement.     Caregivers did not use good judgement when a known food allergen was served in an infant classroom where an infant with that specific diagnosed food allergy was present. Although food wasn't directly served to the infant, the infant was sitting at a table with other children eating the food allergen. Shortly after, the child started experiencing symptoms an allergic reaction.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: AP Background ck determination - If provisionally eligible w/conditions or eligible w/conditions you must restrict duties per conditions/restrictions: Based on information gathered, a caregiver whose background check is provisionally eligible with conditions was left alone with children in a classroom. This was corrected when a caregiver with an eligible background check returned to the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background ck determination - If provisionally eligible w/conditions or eligible w/conditions you must restrict duties per conditions/restrictions (26 TAC §745.635(3))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children: It was determined that the operation failed to adequately supervise a child in care when they left the child on the playground for approximately 2 minutes by themself when the group returned to their classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering: A child's hands were not washed after diaper changing.     Note: This was corrected at inspection as the caregiver washed the child's hands.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering (26 TAC §746.3417(3))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: A Lysol and a pink disinfect bottle were observed accessible to the children in care as it was located on a top of a child's height bookshelf within their reach.     Note: This was corrected at inspection as the caregiver moved the disinfectant bottles to a high shelf.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk: The operation staff did not generate an incident report at the time a three year old child placed a piece of dissolvable disinfectant tablet in their mouth while in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.701(5))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: The operation staff did not report a situation where a child was placed at risk. The operation staff did not report an incident where a three year old placed a small piece of a disinfectant dissolvable tablet in their mouth while in care that required a call to poison control.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Caregiver did not exercise good judgment when failing to ensure the disinfectant tablet completely dissolved in the water before allowing children to use it, resulting in a three year old placing a small piece of the tablet in their mouth for a couple of seconds.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: The parents of two children involved with an incident on the playground regarding child-on-child contact were not properly informed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance: Based on the information obtained for this investigation, the director failed to communicate truthfully with the parents and attempted to withheld information on two children who had physical contact with each other while on the playground.   Director did not follow up with staff to collect more information on the incident.   Director failed to notify licensing on the incident and neglected to create an incident report.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance (26 TAC §746.1003(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: The lack of supervision enabled two children to display inappropriate sexual behavior on each other while on the playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk: The operation failed to create an  incident report on the specific date and time the incident occurred with two children on the playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.701(5))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: The operation failed to notify licensing on an incident that happen on the playground with two children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent: Information gathered for this investigation determined an incident report was not shared with the parent when a child was found unsupervised in the pre-school playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent (26 TAC §746.707)

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: The operation failed to notified licensing on a toddler who wandered off to the preschool playground and was on the play structure that is not age appropriate.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Free of other activities (26 TAC §746.1203(6))

occurrences.finding: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk: Information gathered for this investigation determined a licensing incident report was not created for the child who was found unsupervised on the preschool playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.701(5))

occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: A caregiver was observed out of ratio when observed caring for 18 children. The three year old ratio is 1 to 15.    Note: This was corrected it at inspection as another caregiver stepped in the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: The wooden fence observed dividing the playground space is not in good repair with many wooden boards missing and gates not properly attached to the wooden beams.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - No Pinch, Crush, or Shear Points: The plastic steps on the playscape were observed broken as gaps were seen where children stepped on to them.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - No Pinch, Crush, or Shear Points (26 TAC §746.4601(7))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: Nails were observed protruding from the broken wooden fences that divides the playground spaces.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Hazards Removed or Repaired: Hazards were not removed or repaired promptly after noticing the hazards during their required active play inspections.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Hazards Removed or Repaired (26 TAC §746.4751(c))

occurrences.finding: Report Number of Employees: A review of the Employees Who Left Employment in 2021 data from February 23, 2022, revealed that the center had not reported the number of employees who left employment in 2021 by February 22,2022, as required.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Number of Employees (26 TAC §746.303(b))

occurrences.finding: Report Outbreak of Communicable Illness: The operation did not report two positive COVID cases to Child Care Regulation within 48 hours
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Outbreak of Communicable Illness (26 TAC §746.305(a)(4))
